context: Prep note. Prospect: Northwind Foods, a grocery chain with 14 stores. Contact: Maya Stern, head of e-commerce. They want an online store with delivery slots. The intake form says budget $5,000. They hope to launch before the holiday season. Our standard store build takes 6 weeks and needs the product list first.

lines.text: Hi Maya, thanks for making time. I saw Josh is on the line too.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Hi Dan. Yes, Josh runs operations, so he will join for the delivery questions.
Great. Let me start with what you have in mind for the store.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: We are a grocery chain with fourteen stores and we want customers to order online and pick a delivery slot.
Okay, that is clear. Tell me a bit about how orders reach the stores today.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Today it is all phone calls and a shared spreadsheet, which is a mess honestly.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: So the first thing I need to know is how long it takes to build something like this.
It depends on the scope and mostly on how fast we get your product list.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Understood. Our target is to be live before the holiday season, so we are tight.
Good to know. What is the rough budget you set for this?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: The head office approved around $12,000 for the whole project.
That helps, thank you. Tell me how many products you plan to list.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: About four thousand SKUs, but only a third are available online at launch.
Okay, so around thirteen hundred products at launch.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Right. And I would like to know if you can connect to our inventory system.
I would have to look at how your inventory system exposes its data before I say yes.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Fair enough. Josh, do you remember who the vendor of the inventory system is?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: It is an old on-premise system from a vendor that closed. I will find the manual.
While Josh looks, let me ask about the delivery slots. How do you want them to work?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Customers choose a two hour window and each store has a limit per window.
That is a good model. We can build the limits per store.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Also, I would like to know what a typical go-live checklist looks like.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Also, honestly, we got another quote from a bigger agency and it is much cheaper than I expected.
I would like to see what is included in that quote before we compare.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Sure, I can forward it. Their price is nearly half of what you would charge, and that worries my boss.
Let us compare line by line, then your boss can decide with the full picture.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Okay. Ilan, my boss, makes the final call on this.
Understood. Would Ilan join the next call?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Maybe. And just to be sure, will you also handle hosting and maintenance after launch?
Yes, we have a hosting and maintenance plan, and I will outline it in the proposal.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Did you see the football game last night? I could not sleep after that finish.
I did, what a finish. My neighbours were shouting at the screen.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: I saw the second half only. The coffee this morning is not enough for me.
Same here, I am on my third cup.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Okay, back to work. Josh, can you send me the delivery zone file?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Sure, I will send it to you after the call.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Dan, can you send me a sample proposal as well?
Of course, I will include a sample with the proposal.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: By the way, we also run a loyalty app. Maybe we can talk about it later.
Let us park the loyalty app and finish the store first.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: One more thing, do you take card payments and how does the store handle card data?
We use a payment provider so card data never touches your server.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Good. Regarding timing, we actually need to launch in four weeks.
Four weeks is tight. It depends on getting your product list early.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I will send the full product list by Wednesday, I promise.
Perfect. Then I will send you the proposal by Friday.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Dan, one more thing from me. Do you also handle pickup lockers at the stores?
Let me come back to that one in a moment. First, Josh, can you send me the inventory manual?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: I found the manual, I will email it today.
Great. To summarise, you send the product list by Wednesday and I send the proposal by Friday.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes. And please include a line about the maintenance plan.
Will do. Thanks both, speak soon.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Thanks Dan, bye.
